posts.title: What changes on 7 Dec 2026
posts.summary:
CCDV-F and CCAR-P move to new guides on 7 Dec; CCAR-F does not change.
New format: 70 items (60 scored), scenario-based, same 120 minutes and 720 pass mark.
Booked before 7 Dec: old guide. On or after: new guide plus the new topics.

items: CCAR-F (Architect Foundations): unchanged. The new guide version only touched registration and support wording.
CCDV-F (Developer Foundations): changes on 7 Dec. A new guide takes over.
CCAR-P (Architect Professional): changes on 7 Dec. A new guide takes over, and CCAR-F is the recommended preparation.
CCDV-P (Developer Professional): a new exam, but not a 7 Dec change. Its guide (v1.0) is the same before and after that date.
The video also says Associate Foundations changes that day. This app does not cover that exam.
Changed: 70 items, of which 60 are scored and 10 are unscored trial items you cannot spot. Before: 53 (CCDV-F) and 63 (CCAR-P), all scored.
Changed: items are scenario-based multiple choice, and each item says how many answers to pick.

Changed: domain weights move. CCDV-F Applications and Integration drops from 33.1% to 20%; Evaluation rises from 2.6% to 10%; Claude Code from 3.1% to 8%. CCAR-P Stakeholder Communication halves from 14% to 7%; Integration rises from 19% to 21%.
Same: 120 minutes, pass mark 720 out of 1000, fees ($125 CCDV-F, $175 CCAR-P).
Pacing: 70 items in 120 minutes is about 1 min 43 s per item. Answer every item, since the unscored ones look the same.
Sitting the exam before 7 Dec: keep preparing from the current guide (the one in force through 6 Dec). The new rules do not apply to you.
Sitting it on or after 7 Dec: prepare from the new guide. Your existing study still holds; add the new topics below.
Not booked yet: pick the date first, because the date decides which guide applies.
Evaluation design: golden sets, regression tests, an LLM judge checked against human labels.
Integration resilience: streaming end events, error classes (rate-limit, overloaded, invalid, timeout), Files API.
Grounding and citation: answer from supplied documents, cite them, and say 'not found' when it is not there.
Claude Code extension: choose between a Skill, plugin, rules, hook, subagent or command, and package it.
Cost diagnosis: find the dominant cost driver, use layered or rolling cache breakpoints and batch.
Deployment surface and agent runtime: API vs Bedrock, Vertex or Foundry; Messages loop, Agent SDK or Managed Agents.
Delegation: which steps go to Claude and which stay with people, by reversibility, stakes and accountability.
Reliability controls: rate limits, retry and backoff, idempotency for side effects, fallback routing.
Cache breakpoints, reasoning effort and context lifecycle (editing, memory tool, compaction).
Model version migration: pin, re-tune prompts, re-baseline evals or defer.
LLM-as-judge bias (position, verbosity, self-preference, drift) and trials per case.
Prompt injection surface: retrieved docs, tool results, MCP responses, third-party Skills.
Compliance as architecture (residency, retention, PII redaction, audit logs, tenant isolation) and keeping human ownership of AI-written code.
Nothing to add for 7 Dec. It is a separate exam: 70 items (60 scored), 120 minutes, $175, pass 720, 8 domains. Developer Foundations is recommended first.
